liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Truckin'** (1 review): Harmony vocals in Truckin' are well off key, though Jerry's playing compensates [3]
- **Deal** (1 review): Deal comes early in the show and is singled out as nice [4]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Good Lovin' is called epic, possibly the best version [5]
- **Around and Around** (1 review): Reviewer calls Around and Around the best they ever heard, following the chair clearing [10]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Uncle John's Band is jammed out at length, though the singing isn't harmonious [7]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Jerry sounds great in Lovelight, but Weir's interjections clash with him [7]

## The recordings

- **gd71-03-20.sbd.barbella.5582.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 135 min; rated 3.94/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals seem to distort at louder levels; the reviewer otherwise finds the sound and playing really good; Reviewer says the soundboard sounds great; Jerry's guitar is very loud in the mix [4][7][11]

## Around the show

- Wooden chairs on the Iowa City Fieldhouse floor caused trouble; Jerry stopped the band and asked everyone to stack them against the walls [9]
- Late in the second set, the crowd of about 12,000 passed thousands of wooden chairs overhead to clear the dance floor [10]
- The New Riders opened the show [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-03-20.sbd.barbella.5582.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Mandrake and Steve Barbella; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer sat beside a full soundboard rig and suggests the vaults hold the definitive show; this circulating copy is incomplete [12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Worthpoint: [Grateful Dead Iowa Field House 1971 Concert Poster | #28595731](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-iowa-field-house-1971-concert) [15]
